dual.title: Double extraction
dual.intro: Two people extract the same data independently (tables A and B). The workbench compares them with the engine, shows the disagreements, and for each disagreement you decide – with a reason – which value is correct. The decisions produce the consensus table that the engine will analyse.
dual.noOutcomes: The project has no outcome yet. Add one on the Project screen first.
dual.file.title: Extractor {side} table
dual.file.templateTitle: The header and the study identifiers without values: send this to the second extractor, who fills it in on their own machine.
dual.file.raterHelp: The initials (e.g. SzK) go into the consensus file and the log – never a name or e-mail address. The second extractor works on their own machine (file exchange): send them the template, then import the returned CSV as B. The file is stored byte-for-byte in its own format in the kettos/ folder.
dual.import.readError: The file could not be read
dual.import.replaceBody: Table {side} already exists with different content. If the file you chose is the correct one you can replace it; earlier decisions based on the old values become "stale" and must be decided again.
dual.import.done.same: Table {side}: the same file was already there (no change)
dual.inbox.title: Received files
dual.inbox.help: If you copied the second extractor's file into {dir}, you can import it from here with one click.
dual.sum.title: Agreement (engine comparison)
dual.sum.fieldsCaption: Agreement by column: compared and differing cells; Cohen's κ for categorical and ICC(A,1) for numeric columns, with 95% CI (engine text)
dual.methods.title: Agreement – Methods text (from the engine)
dual.methods.help: The agreement of double extraction must be reported in the manuscript. The engine composed this text from the numbers above; copy it and check it.
dual.key.title: Matching key
dual.key.help: The key tells which row of A belongs to which row of B (e.g. study ID + arm). Choose only columns present in both tables that are unique per row.
dual.key.none: Select at least one key column.
dual.why.gate.asks: Has every disagreement received a reasoned decision before you close the data-extraction stage?
dual.why.gate.because: The purpose of double extraction is to catch errors. If a disagreement stays unresolved, nobody knows which value goes into the analysis – so while one exists, the S08 PASS cannot be recorded (X009).
dual.why.gate.change: Once every disagreement is decided the flag disappears and the consensus table can be written.
dual.st.open.title: Differs and has no decision yet
dual.st.decided.title: A reasoned decision exists
dual.st.stale.title: A or B changed since the decision: decide again
dual.st.auto.title: Same number, different notation (e.g. 1,204 and 1204): no decision needed
dual.items.none: No disagreements: every compared cell matches.
dual.items.keys: Keys: ↑/↓ move, Enter details, A / B quick choice
dual.kind.missing_a: Cell A is empty, B has a value.
dual.kind.missing_b: Cell B is empty, A has a value.
dual.kind.parse: One value cannot be read as a number.
dual.why.x10.asks: Could one value be a typo or a different unit?
dual.why.x10.because: One value is exactly ten times the other. This is almost always a decimal error (4.2 instead of 0.42) or a unit difference (mmol/l vs mg/dl, mm vs cm).
dual.why.x10.change: Check the source (table, footnote, unit). If the paper shows the smaller value, choose it; if the unit differs, enter the converted number as your own value and name the source in the reason.
dual.why.se_sd_swap.asks: Could one extractor have entered the standard error (SE) and the other the standard deviation (SD)?
dual.why.se_sd_swap.because: One value is about √n times the other – exactly the relation between SD and SE (SD = SE·√n). Papers often write "±" without saying which one it is.
dual.why.se_sd_swap.change: Check the table header or footnote for SD or SE. The table needs the SD; if the paper reports the SE, use the converter (SE → SD) and enter that as your own value.
dual.why.arms_swapped.asks: Could the two arms (treatment and control) have been swapped?
dual.why.arms_swapped.because: The treatment value in A sits in the control column in B and vice versa. This would reverse the direction of the effect.
dual.why.arms_swapped.change: Check in the source which group received the intervention. Decide the same way for every affected field of the row (e1/e2, n1/n2) and describe in the reason how you identified the arms.
dual.why.format_only.asks: Is it really the same number?
dual.why.format_only.because: Both cells describe the same number in different notation (thousands separator, decimal comma, trailing zero). The engine does not treat this as a disagreement.
dual.why.format_only.change: No decision is needed: the consensus table keeps A's notation.
dual.why.parse.asks: What exactly is in the cell?
dual.why.parse.because: One value cannot be read as a number (e.g. "NR", "<0.001", text, or two numbers in one cell). The engine cannot compute with it.
dual.why.parse.change: Choose the value that is a number and matches the source; if neither is right, enter the correct number as your own value. If the data is not reported, leave it empty and explain in the reason.
dual.why.category.because: The two extractors chose different categories (e.g. low vs high risk of bias). The engine measures agreement on categorical columns with Cohen's κ.
dual.why.category.change: Re-read the relevant part of the source (or the appraisal form) and choose the better-supported category; cite the source in the reason.
dual.why.missing.asks: Is the value in the source at all?
dual.why.missing.because: One extractor left the cell empty, the other filled it in. One may have missed the value, or the other took it from elsewhere (e.g. supplementary material).
dual.why.missing.change: Look for the value in the source (check the supplement too). If it is there, choose the filled value; if it is not reported, choose the empty one and note where you looked.
dual.why.value.because: The two extractors entered different numbers. The engine shows how much this would move the study's effect size and the pooled estimate – settle the high-impact ones first.
dual.why.value.change: Open the source (page, table) and choose the matching value. If neither matches, enter the correct one as your own value. Write in the reason where you found it (e.g. "Table 2, page 5").
dual.detail.pick: Pick a disagreement from the list: here you see both values, the engine's hint and impact, and you decide here.
dual.detail.noHint: The engine gave no hint for this one.
dual.detail.fromEngine: computed by the engine; the interface computes nothing
dual.detail.auto: Formatting only: no decision needed; the consensus table keeps A's text.
dual.detail.stale: The value changed since the earlier decision (then: A = {a}, B = {b}). Decide again.
dual.choose.otherValue: Own value (the cell text as it goes into the table)
dual.choose.row.a.only_a: A's version: the row is kept in the consensus
dual.choose.row.b.only_a: B's version: the row is dropped
dual.choose.row.a.only_b: A's version: the row is dropped
dual.choose.row.b.only_b: B's version: the row is kept in the consensus
dual.reason.label: Reason (required)
dual.reason.placeholder: e.g. Table 2 footnote: SD; decimal error in B
dual.reason.help: Briefly state why this value is correct and where you found it. No patient identifiers (ID number, date of birth). The reason goes into the consensus file and the project log; the cell value does not.
dual.decide.noReason: A decision cannot be recorded without a reason: briefly state why this value is correct.
dual.decide.noValue: Enter the value to choose your own value.
dual.conflict.title: Someone else changed the decisions meanwhile – reloaded
dual.write.title: Consensus table
dual.write.help: Once every disagreement is decided, the decisions produce the consensus table (reconciled cells get a "reconciled" provenance). Write it to a separate file in the kettos/ folder, or directly into the outcome's data table used by the analysis.
dual.write.outcome: Take over into the outcome data table ({path})…
dual.write.blocked: {n} disagreement(s) still unresolved: until then the consensus table cannot be written (X009).
dual.write.blockedTitle: The consensus table cannot be written yet
dual.write.noData: The outcome has no data table (ma-projekt.json → data).
dual.write.outcomeBody: The consensus table ({rows} rows, {cells} reconciled cells) replaces {path} and will be used by the analysis. The current content is overwritten; reconciled cells get "reconciled" provenance, other cells keep theirs. Earlier analyses will then show as STALE.
dual.write.outcomeDone: Outcome data table updated from the consensus
dual.tables.aria: The two tables side by side with cell-level differences
dual.tables.help: Values of tables A and B side by side per row. Differing cells also get a symbol (≠ open, ✔ decided, ⟳ stale, = formatting only). Enter or double-click on a differing cell: its decision in the list.
dual.engine.missingTitle: The engine comparison is not available
dual.engine.missingHelp: Importing and exporting tables A/B (the file exchange) works meanwhile; comparison and reconciliation start after the engine is updated.
dual.main.title: Disagreements and decisions
dual.main.help: For each disagreement choose the correct value and give a reason. High-impact disagreements (impact column) come first in engine order or when sorting by impact.
dual.need.title: Both tables are not there yet
dual.need.step1: Import your own table (A), or download the template if the extraction was done on the Extraction screen.
dual.need.step2: Send the blank template to the second extractor, who fills it in independently on their own machine.
dual.need.step3: Import the returned file as B (or copy it into the received folder). The comparison then starts.
dual.leave.title: Unfinished decision
dual.leave.body: You typed a reason but did not record the decision. Leave the screen? The text will be lost.
dual.why.rounding.asks: Do the two values differ only by rounding?
dual.why.rounding.because: The two numbers are very close; the difference may come from rounding (e.g. 12.35 vs 12.4). This rarely changes the result, but you still need to decide which is more precise.
dual.why.rounding.change: Choose the one exactly as reported in the source (with more decimals); note in the reason where you saw it.
dual.why.typo.asks: Could it be a typing error?
dual.why.typo.because: The two values differ in a single digit or in two swapped neighbouring digits (e.g. 29 vs 27, or 92 vs 29). This is a typical typo.
dual.why.typo.change: Check the source and choose the matching value. If neither matches, enter the correct one as your own value.
dual.why.sign.because: One value is positive and the other negative (e.g. for change scores or differences). This reverses the direction of the effect.
dual.why.sign.change: Check how the source defined the change (after − before or the reverse) and decide accordingly; state the definition in the reason.
dual.why.percent.asks: Could one extractor have entered a percentage instead of an event count?
dual.why.percent.because: One value looks like a percentage (e.g. 12.5), the other like a count (e.g. 15 out of 120). The table needs the event count.
dual.why.percent.change: If the source reports only a percentage, convert it back to a count with the converter (and flag it), then enter that as your own value.
dual.why.events.because: According to one value there are more events than people in the group – impossible; a number went into the wrong cell or was mistyped.
dual.why.events.change: Check the event count and group size in the source and choose the correct pair.
dual.detail.title: Disagreement details
